alternatives.label: Mathematical systems, autonomous computation, energy and product design (test candidate)
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by mathematics, programming, algorithms, data, optimisation, machine learning and robotics, with one product-development course and a bounded energy-and-sustainability strand. It does not claim aerospace engineering, flight mechanics, structures, propulsion or experimental testing.
alternatives.concept: Test substantial signals and feedback, robotics, numerical modelling and AI with practical materials, product design, renewable-energy assessment and Earth observation as the strongest response to Aerospace Engineering.
progression: Actual24course schedule passes current offerings,earlier formal prerequisites,4coursesperterm,Year1PPD and advanced floor. Numerical and algebraic foundations are generally earlier; OptimizationMethods may accompany foundational calculus because its formal prerequisite is priorProgramming only. Advisory preferences are considered without inventing hard constraints.

candidates.label: Sustainable aviation, wind energy and environmental transition
candidates.reason: Actual renewable-energy,life-cycle,materials andconsumer-design courses are considered fully. They assess energy and product sustainability without a sustained aerodynamic/structural/propulsion vehicle-design inquiry; adding environmental courses changes the organising subject. This is academic insufficiency,not an offering failure.

candidates.label: Space systems, satellites and mission design
candidates.reason: UCR has no orbital or spaceflight mechanics, rocket propulsion, spacecraft systems, satellite-subsystem, mission-analysis or space-design sequence. General mathematics, AI and robotics cannot support a distinct complete space-systems curriculum.

selection.assessment: Internal mechanical prototype only. Its24course schedule tests the strongest response; actual mathematical/systems/robotics/product/energy contributions are acknowledged, but the completed programme fails the target-level academic comparability test. The all-separate row scaffold is not a finding that mathematical or systems subjects have no partial curricular relationship. No active UCR comparison is approved.

trace: supplies programming, testing and debugging for mathematical models and autonomous-system software
establishes documented physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability technologies

Direct mathematical foundation: single-variable calculus, complex numbers and differential-equation modelling, with analytical and Mathematica work. Matrix/eigenvalue study belongs to the separate Linear Algebra course and is not attributed here.

Complementary physical/material inquiry: mechanical/electromagnetic waves, spectroscopy, material structure, stress/strain and laboratory analysis in sustainability settings; no aerospace-structure design is claimed.
Complementary general data preparation, transformation and visualisation inRwith a research project; aerospace or sensor datasets are not guaranteed.
implements search, global and local optimisation and constraint satisfaction for complex systems
develops algorithms and data structures with performance analysis for efficient technical computation
develops vector spaces, matrices and linear transformations for coupled-system models
studies image and video processing, feature detection and tracking relevant to automated observation without claiming physical instrumentation
implements stable numerical methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations

Direct systems-method connection: continuous/discrete signals, differential or difference equations, Fourier/Laplace/Z-transforms, filtering, sampling and linear feedback; aerospace vehicle dynamics and a state-space syllabus are not assumed.

Complementary engineering-design practice: product mechanisms, user needs, specifications, concept selection, production planning and prototypes where feasible; no guaranteed fabrication, quantitative structural model or aircraft project is assumed.
studies robot kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and manipulation as computational autonomy rather than aircraft dynamics
develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertain measurements and model parameters
implements regression and statistical-learning methods relevant to prediction and operational data

Direct decision-method connection: probabilistic inference, Bayesian and temporal models, decision theory, partially observed policies and multi-agent interaction; no taught aircraft operations or resource-allocation project is assumed.

develops neural-network and deep-learning models for advanced data and image analysis
implements reinforcement-learning agents and neural-network methods for adaptive autonomous behaviour
technically and economically assesses energy demand and solar, wind and bioenergy system designs
